newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia 1996 tourist income up 13 pct to $1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia 1996 tourist income up 13 pct to $1.2 bln.

text.p: Slovenia's tourist income rose to $1.22 billion in 1996, up from $1.08 billion in 1995, the Tourist Association at the Chamber of Economy said on Thursday.
The association said income rose largely due to a significant rise in one-day tourists from neighbouring countries.

"The number of one-day tourists was up by nine percent, consisting mainly of Italians, Croatians and Austrians who come to visit a tourist event or a casino, come for shopping or to buy petrol," Danica Zorko, a consultant at the association told Reuters.
The association said the number of tourists rose 14 percent to 831,426, while the number of domestic tourists eased by two percent to 825,005.

In January this year, the number of tourists was up to 86,000, a two-percent increase compared to the same month last year. The number of foreign visitors increased by 13 percent and represented 48.4 percent of all tourists, while the number of domestic tourists was down by three percent.

"Judging from January figures, I expect tourist income will rise to $1.45 billion in 1997 mainly on account of foreign visitors whose number is steadily increasing because of peace in neigbouring Croatia," Zorko said.

She said, however, the number of domestic tourists was expected to fall for the same reason, as an increasing number of Slovenians planned to spend their summer holidays in the Croatian coastal area. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newroom, 386-61-125-8439
